tsk_01M6WVHQG9X5BFR62WFV3BFGEK.progress: KAN-23: read the diff, ACs and head code; now checking wire contract and refund cap against the code.

F1.claim: POST /payments no longer returns merchant_id: the JSON tag was changed to `merchant`, while api/openapi.yaml still requires merchant_id, so any client that reads merchant_id from the create-payment response now gets an empty field. The change is unrelated to the refund feature.

F10.claim: The refund cap reads refunds.total() and then adds in two separate lock acquisitions, so two concurrent refunds of 600 on a payment of 1000 both pass the check and are both logged, over-refunding the payment by 200.

F11.claim: The new POST /payments/{id}/refunds route is registered but api/openapi.yaml and the README still document only /payments (and healthz), so spec-driven clients and generated SDKs cannot see the refund endpoint; the same drift was upheld for healthz in KAN-22.

F2.claim: The new POST /payments/{id}/refunds route is served but api/openapi.yaml still documents only /payments and /healthz, and README still lists only POST /payments, so the published wire contract does not cover the endpoint this change adds.

F3.claim: Two concurrent refunds on one payment can both pass the cap: Refund calls refunds.total() and then refunds.add() in separate lock acquisitions, so two 60 refunds on a payment of 100 can both be accepted and refund 120.

F4.claim: The new refund response omits refund_ref: refundJSON carries only id, payment_id and amount, so the ledger that keys each posting by refund_ref (INC-031) cannot parse it and will skip postings, skewing the daily balance.

F5.claim: Rename of the payment response field merchant_id to merchant breaks the wire contract: api/openapi.yaml still requires and documents merchant_id, and any consumer reading merchant_id now gets an empty value for every POST /payments response.

F6.claim: The refund cap is checked and then recorded under separate lock acquisitions, so two concurrent refunds on one payment can both read the same total and both be accepted, over-refunding (e.g. two 60 refunds on a 100 payment).

F7.claim: The new POST /payments/{id}/refunds route is registered on the router but api/openapi.yaml still documents only /payments and /healthz, so the served surface has a refund endpoint with no schema or path and spec-driven clients/tooling cannot discover or validate it.

F8.claim: POST /payments now serialises the merchant as JSON key "merchant" instead of "merchant_id", so every client following api/openapi.yaml (which declares merchant_id required) loses the field and the response no longer matches the documented contract. The existing api test decodes into paymentJSON, so it does not notice.

F9.claim: POST /payments/{id}/refunds ignores the Idempotency-Key header entirely: a client retry after a timeout creates a second refund and pays out twice, instead of returning the original refund with 200 as ADR-004 requires.
